html:
SMTO-EXE-0166 — SMTO can't turn documents into PDFs

GUID: 48c7f953-dce2-50a3-8357-aeaae0db2c45
Slug: office-conversion-backend-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO can read and edit Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, but it has no safe way to convert them to PDF in this version. Your document wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to make any edits you need to the document first. Editing works normally; only converting to PDF is unavailable.
  2. Open the finished document in Word, Excel, PowerPoint or a similar app and use its Save As or Export option to save a PDF. Those apps can create the PDF safely on your own computer.
  3. If you need the PDF in the conversation, attach it with Add context. This lets SMTO read or share the PDF you made.

What success looks like

  • You have the PDF from your office app, and SMTO's edits are in the document.

If it still fails

  • There is no setting that turns PDF conversion on, and installing LibreOffice on the Gateway won't change this. If your work depends on SMTO converting files, send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • convert_to_pdf is rejected by both tool availability and the Gateway Office worker because no network-isolated, macro-disabled conversion backend is implemented (office.conversion_backend_unavailable).

What this means

  • The worker explicitly rejects convert_to_pdf because this implementation has no safe conversion backend; capability availability reports the same limitation. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • The worker explicitly rejects convert_to_pdf because this implementation has no safe conversion backend; capability availability reports the same limitation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Office conversion capability separately from structural editing and installed desktop applications.

How to fix it

  • No configuration enables conversion: convert_to_pdf is unconditionally unavailable, and installing LibreOffice does not add a backend. Use structural Office operations, or perform conversion outside SMTO in a separately approved application.
  • Structural editing remains available. No network-isolated, macro-disabled conversion backend is implemented; installing LibreOffice alone does not enable conversion.

Retry and execution caution

  • Structural editing remains available. No network-isolated, macro-disabled conversion backend is implemented; installing LibreOffice alone does not enable conversion.

How to verify the fix

  • A separately supported authorized conversion workflow handles the requirement, or conversion remains explicitly unavailable.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
